liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Warm, ambient Dark Star reaches grating crescendos in the jam before Morning Dew, after the first verse; Dark Star runs well over half an hour including Drums; reminds reviewer of Fantasia's Sorcerer's Apprentice [9][10][13]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Not Fade Away into Hey Bo Diddley and back to Not Fade Away is singled out as top; Not Fade Away into Hey Bo Diddley and back is on the official Steppin' Out release [12][18]
- **Mr. Charlie** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Mr. Charlie as a recommended highlight [7]
- **Good Lovin** (1 review): Good Lovin described as hot [12]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Track listing's last eight songs are misordered; correct order after Morning Dew runs GDTRFB through to Comes a Time, with He's Gone after Uncle John's [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Two Souls In Communion**: rare: 10 archived performances [19]
- **Rockin' Pneumonia**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [19]
- **Hey Bo Diddley**: rare: 5 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-23.sbd.cribbs.17700.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 32 songs; 205 min; rated 4.62/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is clean and clear; Reviewer says the show sounds great; Morning Dew has a scratchy, distorted sound; overall sound-quality problems [7][8][13][14][18]
- **gd1972-05-23.sbd.jackson.smith-GEMS.97816.flac16**: soundboard; 30 songs; 224 min; rated 2.5/5 by 6 [3]
- **gd72-05-23.sbd.unicorn.16750.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 210 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd1972-05-23.sbd.unknown.16089.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 221 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [2]

## Around the show

- Uncle John's Band was the encore [18]
- Uncle John's Band was the encore [1]
- Several songs from this show appear on the 'Steppin' Out, England '72' CD [7]
- Reviewer ranks this show above the long-circulating 5/26 show, the last night of the run [10]
- Reviewer counts this among the best shows of 1972 [12]
- Reviewer prefers the 5/26/72 show for playing and recording quality [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-23.sbd.cribbs.17700.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSR>C>DAT>CD>EAC>WAV>SHN via Andy Lemieux encoded by Sean Cribbs [1]
- **gd1972-05-23.sbd.jackson.smith-GEMS.97816.flac16**: taped by Rex Jackson; transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > 2 track soundboard Reel [3]. Also: Rex Jackson taped it, according to a box symbol and David Lemieux; Bob and Betty handled multitracks; Guessed lineage: Jackson two-track, unknown steps, Jerry Garcia's copy, Will Boswell's copy, then CD [3]
- **gd72-05-23.sbd.unicorn.16750.sbeok.shnf**: source: Lineage (most likely):10" 2-track RM > C > D > C speed corrected, complete 4 disk version via Unicorn [4]. Also: This version is nearly the same source as the other, with another source filling tiny missing holes [15]
- **gd1972-05-23.sbd.unknown.16089.shnf**: source: uncertain (believed to be 10" 2-track reel master>1 cassette generation>DAT> 1 cassette generation>circulation [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Europe '72: Strand Lyceum, London, England May 24, 1972](https://www.dead.net/features/listening-party/europe-72-strand-lyceum-london-england-may-24-1972) [20]
